stem: A public health nurse is helping plan a community cancer-control program and reviews state cancer registry data. Which use of these data is appropriate?

options.A: Identify cancer trends and population groups with higher burden so prevention, screening, and cancer-control resources can be better targeted and evaluated.
options.B: Use the registry to determine with certainty which individual community members will develop cancer in the future.
options.C: Replace clinical screening recommendations for individual clients with population-level registry statistics alone.
options.D: Use the registry primarily to calculate hospital billing charges because cancer registry data have little public-health surveillance value.

rationale: CDC's National Program of Cancer Registries collects population-based information on new cancer cases, including cancer characteristics, initial treatment, and outcomes. Registry data are used to monitor cancer trends, identify patterns and higher-burden groups, guide planning and evaluation of cancer-control programs, help allocate health resources, and advance research. These population-level data support public-health planning but do not predict with certainty which individual will develop cancer and do not replace individualized screening recommendations.
educational_objective: Apply population-based cancer registry data to health-promotion planning by using surveillance trends and disparities to guide and evaluate prevention, screening, and cancer-control efforts without substituting population statistics for individual clinical assessment.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: About the National Program of Cancer Registries; Cancer Data and Statistics
source_version_date: NPCR page 2024-12-31; Cancer Data and Statistics 2026-01-13
source_locator: About NPCR — 'What to know,' 'Background,' and uses of cancer registry data; Cancer Data and Statistics — Overview and uses of U.S. Cancer Statistics
source_claim_supported: CDC states that cancer registry data support monitoring trends, identifying population patterns and high-risk groups, planning and evaluating cancer-control programs, allocating resources, research, measuring prevention/control progress, identifying disparities, and improving outcomes.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — population health, risk-factor identification, screening/prevention planning, and health-promotion activities
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — population cancer surveillance used to target and evaluate prevention and screening programs
correction_summary: Rebuilt the original registry-definition item into an applied public-health nursing scenario. Removed vague claims about hospital quality improvement and state-law reporting that were not necessary to the construct, anchored the answer to current CDC NPCR and 2026 cancer-statistics guidance, and remapped the item from Management of Care to Health Promotion and Maintenance because the tested reasoning concerns population surveillance, prevention, screening, disparities, and cancer-control planning.
audit_findings: Original item was primarily definitional and included weak distractors rather than requiring application of registry data to a nursing/public-health decision.

Current CDC resources directly support using cancer registry data to monitor trends, identify disparities/high-burden groups, plan and evaluate cancer-control programs, allocate resources, and support research.
The final item avoids implying that population surveillance can predict individual cancer occurrence or replace client-specific screening guidance.
Blueprint mapping was corrected to Health Promotion and Maintenance because the scenario centers on population risk surveillance and prevention/screening program planning.
Independent adversarial review found one uniquely correct response with no ambiguity, second answer, cueing, unsupported reporting-law claim, or unresolved source conflict.
